name: nav-dynamic-updates-visual
description: Tests NavGrid updates after blast execution changes terrain

steps.description: Staffed opening (#551): a driller with blasting + drill_rig licence, plus an unmanned drill_rig, are hired/purchased for free at game-open — #553's automatic drill dispatch needs both to ever land an ordered hole.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:1 cols:1 spacing:3 depth:6 diameter:0.089 start:10,10
steps.description: Corrected spacing from 1 to 3 to match the drag (#1072): no stepper clicks precede the drag, so the grid tool's spacing stays at its default 3m (DRILL_GRID_DEFAULT_SPACING_M, balance.ts). This is a 1x1 grid (rows:1 cols:1), so spacing has zero effect on the computed hole position -- a single hole lands at the drag's own (10,10) origin regardless of spacing. Correcting a declared value with no behavioral effect.
#553: drain the ordered plan — the staffed driller/drill_rig lands the single hole well inside this pad (sandbox-measured landing at tick 20).

role: player (issue #515): the old "no UI feature" reasoning is stale — Charge.ts's own header comment records that per-hole charging (gap G3) got a real control, ChargeHoleList's `[data-hole="H1"] [data-action="charge-hole"]`, which fills one hole (instead of all of them) with the panel's current product up to its current stemming: 4 m of boomite, 8 kg.
#554: drain the charge order(s) queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) before continuing.

Wait for H1 to dry before firing, as a player would (#1801). The hole holds water when its charge lands (tick 51), and wet boomite fizzles at a tenth of its energy; under the kernel energy model that tenth, spread over the rock around the hole, breaks nothing (the old model still cleared 7 voxels), so the blast below would leave the terrain -- and the NavGrid this file is about -- untouched. The hole dries within ~41 ticks.

expect.note: The dry shot clears 164 voxels around (10,10), so the NavGrid has real terrain change to rebuild; it also kills the driller and blaster at the hole and destroys the drill_rig (#1) and charging truck (#5) parked there.

steps.description: Purchase a vehicle and send it across the grid — its position should advance tick by tick via the NavGrid-aware pathfinding stepper. staffed:true's fleet is 5 vehicles (drill_rig, debris_hauler, rock_digger, rock_fragmenter, charging truck; ids 1-5), and the blast above destroyed the drill_rig and the charging truck parked inside its radius, so this new debris_hauler becomes #6 and brings the count from 3 to 4.

#947: canTickVehicle now requires a driver aboard to advance on tick at all, so hauler #5 needs a driver boarded before the move step below can succeed. Employee #3 (Gus Pickaxe, staffed:true's driving.truck driver) is free -- the driller/blaster/other two drivers never touch this vehicle -- and boards it as its continuity driver (VehicleReservation.ts's driverId===employee.id tie-break), matching the pattern hauling-gate.json already uses for a bootstrap `vehicle driver` assignment.

Employee #3 spawns near the staffed fleet's cluster (~0,2); hauler #5 spawns at (35,35), ~48 tiles away -- confirmed live: 60 ticks is enough for #3 to walk over and board (`vehicle list` shows driver:#3 afterward).

#1895: the explosives delivery wait moves the event clock, so an event can be pending after the tick above and its dialog would cover the Fleet panel; resolved through the event dialog's own buttons, only when one is pending.

Real click path via the shared in-scene move pick (#1766, no hover): click the entity, press the inspector's Move action (arms the tile pick on the entity's own tile), pick tile and confirm. timeout raised from the 60s default (#1092 visual-tester finding): dispatch is proven correct within budget every run (commandOutput "Vehicle #5 repositioning to (15,16).") -- driver #3 is already aboard at this point (boarded during the earlier `tick 60` step), so `vehicle reposition`'s `vehicleDriverId(vehicle) ?? findAvailableDriverForReposition(...)` short-circuits on the already-known driver and never runs #1092's new driver search. Historically what overran the 60s ceiling under `--screenshots` was capture cost (5 captures at ~6s/frame software rasterization, so 3 of 4 shots on a slow sandbox); since #1224 capture time no longer counts against a step's deadline, and the raised 120s timeout is kept as historical headroom with zero change to what is asserted. Never adjust the camera focus offset arithmetically -- re-measure.

expect.note: vehicle list confirms real NavGrid-aware movement toward (15,15) — position advances from spawn each tick

steps.description: Final state dump — vehicle should have advanced toward its destination along the NavGrid path.
